scope: Measured word boundaries for the completed-result and shared-budget regressions. Renewed scenes use their own zero origin. The retained shared-budget scene keeps its original timing and provenance.

changed.previousSay: A controller alternates inspection actions with bounded observations. A line printed by the interpreter can be debugging text or an unfinished answer. Our host therefore keeps it partial and continues the investigation. Completion needs a declared record that the controller can recognize reliably.

The host checks an object, the Boolean value true, and nonempty candidate text. A string in the ready field fails this contract. The later typed record passes and carries the date with its source pointer. This finishes the control loop; factual support is checked separately against the original passage.

Three children repeat the same expiry because all cite one manual page. Their report count grows, while the unique source count remains one. Check what the source establishes and preserve its parentage. Repeated descendants cannot supply additional independent confirmation of the date.

Another applicable policy record gives a different expiry for the same exception. Our structured fixture now returns conflict. It has no precedence rule that resolves these records. The parent preserves that disagreement for investigation rather than converting several confident reports into a majority vote.

Scanning each record grows with the record count. Comparing every unordered pair grows much faster. Watch the same pool expand in both calculations. External storage changes access to the manual; the relationships required by the task still determine how much checking is needed.

Finally compare routes on the same held-out tasks. In these supplied results, direct context misses recall, recursion exceeds cost and latency, and the REPL-only controller clears every gate. Choose an eligible route or hold when none qualifies. Account for actual work and keep the evidence accessible throughout the investigation.

For N records, unordered pairs number N times the quantity N minus one, divided by two. Constant answer-relevant information can still require a search, scanning all records grows linearly, and inspecting all pairs grows quadratically. These describe required information processing, not measured API latency. For a full binary merge tree with L leaves, each internal merge combines two children, so there are L minus one merges and two L minus one requests. The article first plans forty thousand source tokens in sixteen leaves of about twenty-five hundred tokens, giving thirty-one calls. Complete instructions, merge inputs and output reserve must also fit. A model window is not the source allowance.

The executed example instead uses characters. Its five-thousand-seven-hundred-character source, five-hundred-twelve-character window and thirty-two-character reserve produce sixteen leaves and thirty-one requests. The largest input plus reserve is four hundred seven characters. Its fake model returns a sixteen-character digest, not a semantic summary. Reducing the window to two hundred fifty-six gives thirty-two leaves and sixty-three calls; sixty-four cannot fit a merge and is rejected before calls.

A separate exact two-field fixture checks the required date and audit condition. One correct field out of two is recall one half. Fixing the date makes both correct; dropping the condition leaves one half again. Adding an extra false statement does not lower that required-field recall, so inspect unsupported claims separately. Splitting a clause mid-word or losing its qualifier can break semantic preservation even when every character passes through a request.

Bound the whole serialized history as well as one observation. The article keeps a four-hundred-nine-character raw return externally and makes a forty-character preview. The exact marker dot-dot-dot bracket truncated bracket occupies fourteen characters inside the cap, leaving twenty-six characters of source prefix. For smaller limits, even the marker is shortened. The full source remains available through its pointer.

Twenty complete returns contribute eight thousand one hundred eighty characters; twenty previews contribute eight hundred. Neither is a constant-size accumulated history. Code, metadata, wrappers, instructions and reserved output add more. Count the actual tokenizer over the complete next request before every call. Compaction loses details, so retain the mission, inspected source spans and required fields outside the compacted history.

The executed outer-loop fixture uses fixed peek and finish actions, not generated Python or a real model. It returns a candidate after two steps. Repeated peeks hit its step bound; a tighter serialized-history cap yields a distinct history-budget stop. Keep partial findings partial at either limit. Persistent interpreter sessions and trajectory logs do not establish durable distributed checkpointing; scope sessions to the current tenant and source authorization.

beats.say: Depth alone leaves the amount of work open. A controller can take several turns, retry or launch more children. Give the whole tree one shared ledger. Watch the root reserve capacity before dispatch. When actual usage becomes known, reconciliation releases the unused part of its cost estimate.

A child now times out with an unknown provider outcome. Its reservation stays charged. Another child completes and is reconciled. The final request asks for more capacity than remains, so it stays queued. Releasing the unknown reservation early could promise capacity that the timed-out request still consumes.

The host enforces admission, execution limits and deadlines. Generated code cannot award itself a larger budget. The cost units here are supplied teaching estimates; real reservations need valid upper bounds. A private interpreter namespace organizes state, while the executor supplies the actual isolation boundary.
The interpreter can print a date and a citation while it is still searching. That printed line belongs in the working history. Our host looks for a separate answer record before it ends the loop.

Here is the answer record. The content names page six. Look at the quotation marks around false. Our host needs a dictionary, a ready field equal to Boolean true, and nonempty text. Can this record leave the loop?

The quotes make false a string. The host rejects it with a missing Boolean ready signal. Keep the content exactly as it was. Change just the ready field to Boolean true. Run the same check again. This time the host returns the candidate. Now verify the date against its source.

One child read page six. Two more children cite the same page. Follow their citations. All three lines end at one source. Counting the reports as three votes would give that page three times the influence. Ask each child to look for an applicable policy, including one that could overturn the date.

A fourth reader brings back an October date. Read the scope beside it. This one covers billing exports. Set it aside for a legacy-token question. When checking structured records, discard unknown IDs, count a repeated ID once, and keep records that apply to the claim. If none remain, ask for evidence.

Replace that fourth citation with the bulletin below. The bulletin covers the very same legacy-token exception. The dates disagree and we have no rule giving either source priority. Can we certify September thirtieth?

One applicable record says September thirtieth. The other says October fifteenth for the same exception. In this exact-field check the result is conflict. Leave the date unresolved. Find out which policy governs this run before clearing it.

Four records take four visits to scan. If you must compare every pair, read the lit squares. Each pairs one record with a different record. Leave out the diagonal and count only one side. Now double the record count. For eight records, each has seven possible partners. Divide by two because each pair has two ends. That gives twenty-eight pairs. Ten thousand records give nearly fifty million pairs before pruning. Relationships are work to account for. They need not each become a model call. Even a single fact can take a search to find.

To choose a route, compare all three on the same labeled questions. These are invented results. Require recall of at least point nine, a ninety-fifth percentile cost of at most thirty cents per task, and a ninety-fifth percentile latency of at most twelve seconds. Which route clears all three limits?

Direct is cheap, but its recall is only point seven three. The recursive route crosses both the time and cost limits. The interpreter working alone clears all three. The policy chooses the lowest-cost eligible route, using lower latency to break a cost tie. If none qualifies, hold deployment. Estimate these percentiles across enough trials, report uncertainty, and enforce separate limits on each live request.

For a full binary tree, every merge turns two results into one. To turn sixteen leaves into one answer takes fifteen merges. In general, L leaves need L minus one merges. Say the manual has forty thousand source tokens. Halve the source until each leaf fits. Sixteen leaves of about twenty-five hundred tokens give thirty-one requests, provided each complete leaf and merge fits the window.

Now switch units. This run splits fifty-seven hundred characters and returns a sixteen-character digest from each call. In a window of five hundred twelve, eighteen characters of instruction and thirty-two of output reserve leave four hundred sixty-two for source. Halving gives sixteen leaves and thirty-one requests. The largest input plus reserve is four hundred seven characters. At half the window, the same source needs thirty-two leaves and sixty-three requests. At sixty-four characters even a merge cannot fit. Reject that setting before the first call.

The digest tells us the requests ran. To check meaning, take a separate candidate with the correct condition and the wrong date. One match out of two gives recall of one half. Correct the date and both fields match. Now remove the condition. Only one match remains. Add an unsupported claim and that score stays put. It counts the required fields only. Check extra claims separately, and keep clauses together when splitting the text.

Keep this raw observation outside the prompt. It is four hundred nine characters long. Make a forty-character preview for the next turn. The truncation marker takes fourteen of those characters. That leaves twenty-six for the source text. If the cap is shorter than the marker, shorten the marker too. Keep the pointer so the controller can reopen the full observation.

Keep taking observations of the same size. At twenty returns, compare the two totals. The full returns occupy eight thousand one hundred eighty characters, the previews eight hundred. Both keep growing. Before every call, tokenize the whole input, including code, instructions and wrappers. Add the output reserve before checking the window. If you compact the history, preserve the mission and the evidence pointers outside it.

Here is a small controller with two fixed actions. Peek at the manual, then finish. The second step stores a candidate. Keep peeking instead and the step limit ends the run. Tighten the history limit, and the same peek can exhaust the history budget. Save the partial findings and the actual stop reason. A persistent interpreter can retain variables, and a log records a trajectory. For recovery across processes you still need a saved checkpoint scoped to this user and source.
